findings.title: Deferred color upgrade rewrites the folder's identity from a read taken before the awaits
findings.body: `availability` reads the folder's identity at line 657 (await), then at 681-684 writes `{ ...identity.identity, color: entry.color }`: the whole object from that earlier read, with no re-read and no per-workspace lock. `UPDATE_LOCK` (line 928) serializes only registry updates, not identity-file writes. `edit` probes (line 591), reads the file (596) and writes its name (612) with the same unlocked pattern. Overlap: a probe that read the old Default before `edit`'s write lands its write after it, so the folder's name reverts to "Default workspace" while `edit` has already set the registry name and cleared `pendingIdentity` (630). The next probe sees a different name and takes the folder's (700-708), so the rename is lost with no message. Probes run on every capture (index.ts:113-115), so the overlap is reachable. The same window exists if another Mac writes between the read at 657 and the write at 684. The pendingIdentity branch (663-671) has the same whole-object write. Fix: re-read the identity immediately before writing and write only if it is still the old Default in rose, or serialize identity-file writes per workspace path with `withLock`.

findings.title: Picking the folder a workspace already has reports that it 'now points to the new folder'
findings.body: `relocate.ts:42-43` now returns `{ ok: true }` for the folder the workspace already points at, so `relocateFolder` (index.ts:340-349) answers ok and `onRelocated` shows the toast `folderChanged` ("Done. {name} now points to the new folder.", en.json:2622). Nothing changed, so "new folder" is false. Consider a no-change message, or no toast, for this case.

findings.title: A pending workspace now accepts any folder that has Kaipu items and no identity.json
findings.body: `checkRelocate` returns ok at 848 for any `pendingInit` entry when the picked folder has `.kaipu/` and no identity. The probe after the move (index.ts:342 → registry.ts:724-737) then writes identity.json there under the registered id. Before this change, that folder was refused as `has-items-no-identity` because no workspace could claim it. Now a pre-workspaces library, or another Mac's folder that was never given an identity, can be taken, and its items appear under this workspace. The PR body still lists "`.kaipu/` items but no identity: refused" as a rule, which is now true only for non-pending entries. Is adopting any such folder intended for pending workspaces? The new test (registry-relocate.test.ts:200-219) covers only the moved-folder case. Also: the second half of the open thread on this line (a folder whose identity belongs to another id, registry.ts:835-838) is still refused, so this is a question about the first half only.

contracts.action: Change folder… in the Edit dialog (changeFolder): calls the relocate IPC and handles the result
contracts.before_after: Before: the dialog had no catch, so a rejected IPC call left the button and the error unset. Now: a catch sets folderError to relocateUncertain. Both paths reset relocating in finally. A successful result calls onRelocated, which shows the toast (context:165-170).
contracts.visible_effect: A refusal shows inline (role=alert, workspace-dialog.tsx:252-256). A cancelled picker shows nothing (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:268-275). A rejection shows 'can't tell whether the folder was changed'. The toast from the context shows on success.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection can come after main already applied the new folder (index.ts:340-348), so the message says the result is unknown; nothing is lost. A rejection before the picker (for example showOpenDialog throwing, index.ts:334-336) reports 'unknown' although nothing changed. That is honest but imprecise. The dialog stays open and the button is re-enabled.

contracts.action: relocate on the same folder the workspace already points at (early return)
contracts.before_after: Before: the same folder went through relocateActive (prepare windows, close gate, apply, drop captures, commit, bump generation; switch-transaction.ts:106-133) or registry.relocate (a write). Now: an early return skips all of that. The caller still runs the probe (index.ts:342), refreshTitles and broadcastState (index.ts:344-345).
contracts.visible_effect: No window is asked to save, no capture is dropped, no route remounts. The success toast still shows (see the consider finding).
contracts.failure_mode: None in the transaction. If the probe rewrites the identity and fails, the caller already ignores that (registry.ts:743-747). The early return runs only after checkRelocate, so an identity belonging to another id is still refused first (registry.ts:835-838).

contracts.action: relocate a pendingInit workspace to a folder with Kaipu items and no identity.json
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:711-721 (availability adopts a pendingInit entry's folder) and 724-747 (availability writes the file under the registered id)
contracts.before_after: Before: any folder with .kaipu/ and no identity was refused as has-items-no-identity. Now: pendingInit entries accept it. The path changes, then the probe (index.ts:342) writes identity.json under the registered id and clears pendingInit (registry.ts:736-741).
contracts.visible_effect: The row becomes connected with the workspace's old name and color, and the folder's Kaipu items appear in the library.
contracts.failure_mode: If the probe's write fails (for example a read-only folder), pendingInit stays set, relocate has already reported ok, and availability still returns available (registry.ts:743-747). The identity is then never written, and nothing tells the user. Also see the question finding on this line about which folders may be taken.
contracts.open_question: Is it intended that a pendingInit workspace adopts any folder with Kaipu items and no identity, such as a pre-workspaces library? Is a failed identity write after a successful relocate meant to stay silent?

contracts.action: Deferred color upgrade written to the folder when it reconnects (availability)
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade used pendingIdentity, which writes the registry's full name and color. Now: pendingColorUpgrade writes only the color, and only if the file read at 657 is still the old Default in rose. The flag is cleared after the write (685).
contracts.visible_effect: The folder takes the new color on reconnect. A folder changed on another Mac is adopted instead (700-708).
contracts.failure_mode: A write between the read (657) and the write (684) is overwritten, and the same happens to a concurrent edit (see the fix finding on line 684). No lock covers identity writes.

contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:257-260 (open, which calls it) and 457 (availability for the owner)
contracts.before_after: Before: the marker and pendingIdentity were set in one write. Now: pendingColorUpgrade is set instead, then availability(owner.id) runs when the folder is reachable.
contracts.visible_effect: The registry shows kaipu at once. The folder follows on reconnect.
contracts.failure_mode: If the marker write fails, it is logged and retried at the next launch (452-455). Nothing is lost, and the upgrade is not applied to the folder until the probe runs.

contracts.action: Create and edit rejected by IPC: dialog shows an uncertain message
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/workspaces/workspace-dialog.tsx:124 and 128 (the refusal branches of the same submit)
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection was unhandled, and busy was reset only in finally. Now: a catch sets create-uncertain or edit-uncertain, and finally still resets busy.
contracts.visible_effect: An alert with the uncertain text (refusalMessage, workspace-dialog.tsx:337-362). The button is re-enabled. The dialog stays open.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected create may already have registered the workspace. A retry is refused as 'exists' (registry.ts:509) or by name, so it does not duplicate. A throw from onCreated or onSaved inside the try would be reported as uncertain. That case is unlikely.

contracts.action: Change folder rejected by IPC: context shows a toast
contracts.before_after: Before: the context called the IPC without a catch. Now: a try/catch shows relocateUncertain and returns. The success path is outside the try, so onRelocated errors are not reported as uncertain.
contracts.visible_effect: A toast 'can't tell whether the folder was changed'.
contracts.failure_mode: The same as the dialog's: an unknown result, nothing lost. The workspace list refreshes only if main broadcast (index.ts:345).

thread_replies.reply: Addressed: the rollback at registry.ts:636-640 removes the file when the folder had none (`previous.kind === "absent"`) as well as restoring the old one.
Addressed: edit re-runs the name check inside the locked update (registry.ts:619-621) and throws NameTakenError, so two concurrent edits cannot both take a name.
Addressed: refusalMessage takes `editing`, and edit refusals use editNotWritable and editFailed (workspace-dialog.tsx:337-362). The test asserts the exact text (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:454-456).
Addressed: the late answer now resolves inside `await act(...)` (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:163-166), so the stale-answer test fails without the alive guard.

Partly addressed. The no-identity half is handled at registry.ts:843-848. The other half is not: a folder whose identity has another id still returns `different` at registry.ts:835-838, although availability adopts that id for a pendingInit entry (registry.ts:711-721). See the new question finding on line 848.

Addressed: relocate.ts:42-43 returns early when the picked folder is the one the workspace already points at, so no window is asked to prepare and no capture is dropped. The caller's probe still runs.
Addressed: the "Move to" sentence is gone from en.json:2623 and es.json:2623, and the dialog test now asserts it is absent (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:294).

Addressed: a rejected relocate sets relocateUncertain in the dialog (workspace-dialog.tsx:147-150) and in the context (workspaces-context.tsx:177-180). It is 'uncertain' rather than 'failed' because the rejection can come after main applied the new folder.
Addressed: the test now relocates, checks Save is still disabled, then changes the color and checks Save is enabled (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:343-355).

structuredOutput.summary: Reviewed the 10 files of this part (registry.ts, relocate.ts, the dialog and context, their tests, and the en/es messages). Main findings: (1) a race in availability's deferred-color-upgrade write (registry.ts:684), which can overwrite a concurrent edit's rename without lock or re-read; (2) the same-folder early return makes the success toast say "now points to the new folder" when nothing changed; (3) a question on whether pendingInit workspaces should adopt any folder with Kaipu items and no identity.json. Thread status: the registry.ts:809 thread is only partly addressed (the no-identity half is fixed; the other-id half is still open); the relocate no-op, Move-to copy, rejected-relocate, and dialog test threads are addressed, as are the earlier create/edit rollback, lock, refusal-copy and act() threads. Threads on other parts' files (workspace-name, index.ts, switch-transaction, the ADR) are outside this part and not answered here. Read-only review; nothing was built or run.

findings.title: Deferred color upgrade rewrites the folder's identity from a read taken before the awaits
findings.body: `availability` reads the folder's identity at line 657 (await), then at 681-684 writes `{ ...identity.identity, color: entry.color }`: the whole object from that earlier read, with no re-read and no per-workspace lock. `UPDATE_LOCK` (line 928) serializes only registry updates, not identity-file writes. `edit` probes (line 591), reads the file (596) and writes its name (612) with the same unlocked pattern. Overlap: a probe that read the old Default before `edit`'s write lands its write after it, so the folder's name reverts to "Default workspace" while `edit` has already set the registry name and cleared `pendingIdentity` (630). The next probe sees a different name and takes the folder's (700-708), so the rename is lost with no message. Probes run on every capture (index.ts:113-115), so the overlap is reachable. The same window exists if another Mac writes between the read at 657 and the write at 684. The pendingIdentity branch (663-671) has the same whole-object write. Fix: re-read the identity immediately before writing and write only if it is still the old Default in rose, or serialize identity-file writes per workspace path with `withLock`.

findings.title: Picking the folder a workspace already has reports that it 'now points to the new folder'
findings.body: `relocate.ts:42-43` now returns `{ ok: true }` for the folder the workspace already points at, so `relocateFolder` (index.ts:340-349) answers ok and `onRelocated` shows the toast `folderChanged` ("Done. {name} now points to the new folder.", en.json:2622). Nothing changed, so "new folder" is false. Consider a no-change message, or no toast, for this case.

findings.title: A pending workspace now accepts any folder that has Kaipu items and no identity.json
findings.body: `checkRelocate` returns ok at 848 for any `pendingInit` entry when the picked folder has `.kaipu/` and no identity. The probe after the move (index.ts:342 → registry.ts:724-737) then writes identity.json there under the registered id. Before this change, that folder was refused as `has-items-no-identity` because no workspace could claim it. Now a pre-workspaces library, or another Mac's folder that was never given an identity, can be taken, and its items appear under this workspace. The PR body still lists "`.kaipu/` items but no identity: refused" as a rule, which is now true only for non-pending entries. Is adopting any such folder intended for pending workspaces? The new test (registry-relocate.test.ts:200-219) covers only the moved-folder case. Also: the second half of the open thread on this line (a folder whose identity belongs to another id, registry.ts:835-838) is still refused, so this is a question about the first half only.

contracts.action: Change folder… in the Edit dialog (changeFolder): calls the relocate IPC and handles the result
contracts.before_after: Before: the dialog had no catch, so a rejected IPC call left the button and the error unset. Now: a catch sets folderError to relocateUncertain. Both paths reset relocating in finally. A successful result calls onRelocated, which shows the toast (context:165-170).
contracts.visible_effect: A refusal shows inline (role=alert, workspace-dialog.tsx:252-256). A cancelled picker shows nothing (workspace-dialog.test.tsx:268-275). A rejection shows 'can't tell whether the folder was changed'. The toast from the context shows on success.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection can come after main already applied the new folder (index.ts:340-348), so the message says the result is unknown; nothing is lost. A rejection before the picker (for example showOpenDialog throwing, index.ts:334-336) reports 'unknown' although nothing changed. That is honest but imprecise. The dialog stays open and the button is re-enabled.

contracts.action: relocate on the same folder the workspace already points at (early return)
contracts.before_after: Before: the same folder went through relocateActive (prepare windows, close gate, apply, drop captures, commit, bump generation; switch-transaction.ts:106-133) or registry.relocate (a write). Now: an early return skips all of that. The caller still runs the probe (index.ts:342), refreshTitles and broadcastState (index.ts:344-345).
contracts.visible_effect: No window is asked to save, no capture is dropped, no route remounts. The success toast still shows (see the consider finding).
contracts.failure_mode: None in the transaction. If the probe rewrites the identity and fails, the caller already ignores that (registry.ts:743-747). The early return runs only after checkRelocate, so an identity belonging to another id is still refused first (registry.ts:835-838).

contracts.action: relocate a pendingInit workspace to a folder with Kaipu items and no identity.json
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:711-721 (availability adopts a pendingInit entry's folder) and 724-747 (availability writes the file under the registered id)
contracts.before_after: Before: any folder with .kaipu/ and no identity was refused as has-items-no-identity. Now: pendingInit entries accept it. The path changes, then the probe (index.ts:342) writes identity.json under the registered id and clears pendingInit (registry.ts:736-741).
contracts.visible_effect: The row becomes connected with the workspace's old name and color, and the folder's Kaipu items appear in the library.
contracts.failure_mode: If the probe's write fails (for example a read-only folder), pendingInit stays set, relocate has already reported ok, and availability still returns available (registry.ts:743-747). The identity is then never written, and nothing tells the user. Also see the question finding on this line about which folders may be taken.
contracts.open_question: Is it intended that a pendingInit workspace adopts any folder with Kaipu items and no identity, such as a pre-workspaces library? Is a failed identity write after a successful relocate meant to stay silent?

contracts.action: Deferred color upgrade written to the folder when it reconnects (availability)
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade used pendingIdentity, which writes the registry's full name and color. Now: pendingColorUpgrade writes only the color, and only if the file read at 657 is still the old Default in rose. The flag is cleared after the write (685).
contracts.visible_effect: The folder takes the new color on reconnect. A folder changed on another Mac is adopted instead (700-708).
contracts.failure_mode: A write between the read (657) and the write (684) is overwritten, and the same happens to a concurrent edit (see the fix finding on line 684). No lock covers identity writes.

contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:257-260 (open, which calls it) and 457 (availability for the owner)
contracts.before_after: Before: the marker and pendingIdentity were set in one write. Now: pendingColorUpgrade is set instead, then availability(owner.id) runs when the folder is reachable.
contracts.visible_effect: The registry shows kaipu at once. The folder follows on reconnect.
contracts.failure_mode: If the marker write fails, it is logged and retried at the next launch (452-455). Nothing is lost, and the upgrade is not applied to the folder until the probe runs.
